objective: Frozen experiment on interacting pair failures (higher layers at gadget characters): on zero-jump gadget knots with dedicated vertex copies and Brunnian insertions at slope d/p, test that the pinned count is an edge-local integer partition function (edge equations independent of non-neighbouring data on the solution variety, vertex pairings vanishing), that the edge count is maximal on the diagonal and strictly smaller across a pair-failing difference, and hence that the edge matrix has rank at least two; with controls (cumulative gadget design; an algebra violating the conditions).
status: Closed: supported under its frozen rule (E002; E001 refuted by an off-variety locality rule and kept). On zero-jump gadgets for five interacting algebras, the edge count is maximal on the diagonal and smaller across a pair-failing difference, vertex pairings vanish, and path locality holds on the solution variety; off-variety data break locality (control X3).
title: Interacting pair failures on zero-jump gadgets: locality, vertex freeness and the Brunnian rank
